description: Find the most load each web variant can hold at a target frame rate, with no cap. For each case, a fresh headless Chromium (real GPU) opens the page with `param` set (e.g. ?lights=100), waits until ready, settles, then counts requestAnimationFrame callbacks. It raises the load ~30% a step until a valid sample misses `targetFps`, confirms the miss, then bisects to within a few percent; if the first load misses it searches down. A page error ends the round as invalid instead of counting as a miss. An app's own capped test is not the ceiling. Needs Playwright in the project. Blocks until done.

cases.description: Variants to ramp, e.g. [{name: 'baseline', params: {variant: 'baseline'}}, {name: 'atlas', params: {variant: 'atlas'}}].

headed.description: Show the browser window (uses the screen's refresh rate). Default false.

maxBatchMs.description: Stop the whole batch after this long. Default 40 minutes.

measureMs.description: How long to count frames per step. Default 2000.

param.description: Query param that sets the load, e.g. 'lights' or 'count'.

precisionPct.description: Bisect until the pass/miss gap is within this percent. Default 4.

readySelector.description: CSS selector that must exist before counting frames.

rounds.description: Ramps per case (1–5); the ceiling is the median of valid rounds. Default 1. Use 3 to settle close calls.

settleMs.description: Wait after ready before counting frames. Default 1000.

targetFps.description: Frame rate each step must hold. Default 55.

url.description: Origin of the running app, e.g. http://localhost:5173

name: find_web_ceiling
